---
title: Agents for your app's users
description: "Giving each user of your app their own Pi Durable Platform agent: service-managed agents by external key with a service account, or agents by key in each person's personal workspace with OAuth Connect."
---

An app often wants **one agent per user**: each person gets their own assistant, with conversations nobody else shares. Pi Durable Platform supports two ways to do it. Agents that hold nothing in common are separate agents; threads of one agent share its tools (see [Private threads](/docs/build/private-threads#what-private-threads-dont-hide)).

Both use the same call, `PUT /v1/teams/{team}/agents/by-key/{key}`: it returns the agent with that **external key**, and creates it the first time.

- The first call creates the agent (`201`); later calls return the same agent (`200`) and ignore the body. It's idempotent: call it whenever you need the agent's ID.
- The external key is 1 to 200 letters, digits or `. _ : @ -`, unique in the team.
- The body is optional: `name` (default: the external key), `description`, `templateId` (a catalog template or one of the team's own, private ones too) or `template` (a platform template's slug; default `assistant`), and `modelId` (a model published to the team).

Who may call it depends on the team.

## With a service account: service-managed agents

Your team creates an **editor** service account and gives your app its key. The app asks for an agent by a key of its choosing, for example its own user ID:

```sh
curl -X PUT https://agents.example.com/v1/teams/support/agents/by-key/u-42 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PDP_SA_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Assistant for user 42", "templateId": "…"}'
```

In a shared team, only **editor** service accounts may call it; people get `403`, whatever credential they use. These agents are **service-managed** (`serviceManaged: true`):

- Only the team's service accounts use them: list them with `GET /v1/agents` or `GET /v1/teams/{team}/agents` with the service account's key.
- The team's members don't see them. Owners and admins see that they exist (name, external key, status, last use), never their conversations, and can delete them.
- They don't count towards the team's limit of 50 agents. There is no platform limit on how many you create; your cluster's capacity bounds how many run at once, and idle ones hibernate.
- Your editor service account can change and delete them (`PATCH` and `DELETE /v1/agents/{agentId}`), but not the team's ordinary agents.
- They can't be [moved](/docs/use/moving-an-agent) to another team.

The conversations belong to your app, not to the people: the platform knows only the service account as the author. Your app decides which user sees which agent.

## With OAuth Connect: agents in personal workspaces

If people connect your app with [OAuth Connect](/docs/build/oauth-connect), keep their agent in their **personal workspace**, with their token. The agent and its conversations are theirs, and they see it in the console like any other agent of the workspace.

```sh
# Find the personal workspace
curl https://agents.example.com/v1/teams -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"   # the team with "kind": "personal"

# Templates and models it may use
curl https://agents.example.com/v1/agent-templates -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
curl https://agents.example.com/v1/teams/$PERSONAL/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# The agent for one purpose, created the first time
curl -X PUT https://agents.example.com/v1/teams/$PERSONAL/agents/by-key/chat-assistant \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Assistant", "templateId": "…", "modelId": "…"}'
```

- In a personal workspace, its owner may call `PUT …/by-key/…` with any of their credentials: a browser session, a personal API key, or an app they connected (scope `agents`). Anyone else gets `404 team_not_found`.
- The agent is the workspace's, **not** service-managed. It counts towards the workspace's `maxAgents`, and the person can rename, change, move or delete it in the console.
- The key names a purpose within the person's workspace (`chat-assistant`, `research`), so your app needn't store the agent's ID. If the person deletes the agent, the next call creates a new one.
- The template must be in the **catalog** (personal workspaces have no templates of their own), and its model, or the `modelId` you pass, must be offered to personal workspaces; otherwise `409 model_unavailable`.
- The workspace's limits apply: `maxAgents` on create (`409 limit_reached`) and `maxRunning` on waking (`409 too_many_running`). Read them from `GET /v1/teams/{team}/limits` rather than assuming the defaults (5 and 2).
- Agents stay on the template version they were made with. To roll out a new version, `PATCH /v1/agents/{agentId}` with `templateVersion`, using the person's token.

You can also create agents with `POST /v1/teams/{team}/agents`. Send an `Idempotency-Key`, so a retry after a timeout returns the first agent instead of making another; see [Creating agents safely](/docs/build/creating-agents). Names are unique per workspace, ignoring case (`409 name_taken`).

## Choosing

| | Service account by key | OAuth Connect in personal workspaces |
|---|---|---|
| Who owns the agent | Your team (service-managed) | The person |
| People must connect | No | Yes, once |
| Visible in the console | To your team's owners and admins, without conversations | To the person |
| Limits | Your cluster | The workspace's `maxAgents` and `maxRunning` |
| Templates | Your team's and the catalog | The catalog |
| Can be moved | No | Yes, by the person ([Moving an agent](/docs/use/moving-an-agent)) |

A keyed agent that is moved loses its key: `PUT …/by-key/{key}` then creates a new agent.
